https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world.text: Germany faces daily hybrid warfare attacks from abroad, interior minister Alexander Dobrindt was quoted as saying on Sunday, following a suspected attack attempt involving an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig/Halle Airport. Dobrindt told the newspaper Bild am Sonntag that foreign powers wanted to subdue Germany politically and socially by stirring up fear there. Dobrindt highlighted the expansion ‌of drone ​research in Germany as part ‌of the response to the ​new threats. “We're not at war, but we are the daily target of hybrid warfare,” Dobrindt said. “Espionage, sabotage, cyberattacks, or covert operations by foreign powers aimed at destabilising Germany or inflicting direct harm are a constant reality.” The newspaper's advance ​release ⁠of the interview did ‌not say whether he identified any countries in particular. After the drone loaded with explosives was discovered at the airport in eastern Germany on Tuesday, some German lawmakers pointed the finger at Russia, which has been at war with Ukraine since its military invasion of the country in 2022. The Russian embassy in Berlin on Friday dismissed the Leipzig event as a "fabricated provocation", saying it was another example of accusations against Russia without evidence.

https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/.text: World Mid-East Europe Americas Asia Pacific Africa Syrian Crisis Islamophobia Zelenskyy says US briefed Ukraine on recent Moscow meetings by Reuters Aug 28, 2026 - 9:58 pm GMT+3 Edited By Nurbanu Tanrıkulu Kızıl Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy speaks during a press conference with Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic (not pictured) following their meeting in Belgrade, Serbia, Aug. 8, 2026. (EPA File Photo) by Reuters Aug 28, 2026 9:58 pm Edited By Nurbanu Tanrıkulu Kızıl Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Friday that Washington had shared intelligence with Kyiv about a series of meetings held in Moscow in recent days. "Today we ⁠received information from the American side about the meetings in Moscow that took place these days. There ​were a number of meetings there," Zelenskyy said ​on ⁠Telegram, without going into detail on who was at the meetings. "I thank them for the information and for the necessary tone of the conversation with Russia," Zelenskyy added, again without elaborating. The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that CIA Director John Ratcliffe had travelled to Moscow to warn Russia off any attack on a NATO member. The Kremlin dismissed the report, while U.S. President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin would not attack a ⁠NATO ⁠country, playing down media reports on Ratcliffe's trip. Two sources told Reuters that Ratcliffe had raised the possibility of a Russian operation against a NATO member during the meeting, although it was unclear whether that was the primary purpose of the trip. The talks also covered Russia's support for Iran, one source told Reuters. Also Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on ⁠Friday that Warsaw was in constant contact with the CIA leadership and was not surprised byRatcliffe's visit to Moscow. "We are not taken by surprise by ​any information regarding the operations and initiatives the CIA Director is conducting," Tusk ​told a youth conference when asked if the visit should be a source of concern. "Poland was also informed ⁠about ‌the need ‌for an urgent discussion on this matter at ⁠the highest possible Polish-American level," Tusk ‌added without elaborating. He said that there have been signals in the public ​domain that Russia is preparing ⁠to escalate tensions, both in the war with ⁠Ukraine and across the region, and that this autumn ⁠and winter are set ​to be pivotal for Russia. shortlink copied KEYWORDS russia-ukraine war volodymyr zelenskyy The Daily Sabah Newsletter Keep up to date with what’s happening in Turkey, it’s region and the world. https://www.dw.com/en/pakistan-president.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5O83e Pakistan's government has been bracing for the arrival of Imran Khan supporters demanding the former PM be released from prison Image: REUTERS Advertisement Pakistan's President Asif Ali Zardari on Sunday announced that the northwestern Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had been put under emergency rule, effectively removing power from former Prime Minster Imran Khan 's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party. The imposition of emergency rule comes as thousands of Khan supporters continue to stage anti-government protests and demand the former leader be released from jail . Current Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif proposed the move, which Zardari signed into order on Sunday. The suspension of regional government was justified under constitutional articles that allow the central government to confront security threats and give it sweeping powers in emergency situations. Sharif's government claims regional authorities have not done enough to curb Islamist violence in the province. Authorities have set up massive roadblocks across Pakistan to keep Khan supporters at bay Image: Abdul Majeed/AFP Why is Pakistan's government taking control of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa? Last Sunday, thousands of Khan's supporters began to make their way from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to the Pakistani capital, Islamabad. Organizers had declared their intent to rally hundreds of thousands more along the way in hopes of bringing about Khan's release from prison. Despite being jailed since 2023, Khan, a popular former cricket star, maintains great influence in Pakistan, with he and his followers convinced that his imprisonment is the result of political persecution. Khan, who began his term as prime minister in August 2018, was ousted from office in April 2022 after losing a no-confidence vote. Khan's supporters want him released from jail Image: Faridullah Khan/DW He has been in prison since August 2023. Beyond corruption and treason charges, he was also accused of inciting violence after widespread anti-government protests in May 2023. Khan rejects the charges as a politically motivated plot to keep him away from power. He remains a popular political figure in Pakistan. Khan's supporters claim that the 2024 election that brought Shehbaz Sharif back to power was rigged — an accusation the government denies. Pakistan has seen a resurgence of terror attacks over the past several months and the Sharif government accuses Khan's PTI of sympathizing with the Pakistani Taliban, also known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, which is largely thought to be behind the attacks. The PTI rejects these accusations as a baseless smear campaign.
